rows.selection_reason: The existing evidence is empty, so the first experiment should test a baseline multimodal configuration to establish performance benchmarks. This experiment tests the impact of multimodal integration (rna + image) with multiprofile settings, using standard encoders (scvi_n200 for RNA, resnet50 for image) and simple aggregation/fusion (avgpool + concat). It clarifies whether multimodal approaches outperform single-modality baselines and isolates the effect of encoder choices, which are critical design decisions.

The existing evidence shows config_001 (multimodal, multiprofile, scvi_n200, resnet50, avgpool, concat) achieves 0.6315 validation accuracy. This experiment tests whether changing the fusion method from concat to weighted (while keeping other parameters identical) improves performance. It isolates the effect of fusion strategy, a critical design choice, without altering multiple parameters, providing direct evidence about its impact on accuracy.

Existing evidence shows weighted fusion (config_027) outperforms concat (config_001). This experiment tests whether replacing the RNA encoder (scvi_n200 → pca_n2000) while retaining the effective weighted fusion and resnet50 image encoder will further improve performance. It isolates the impact of RNA representation choice, a critical design decision, under the promising weighted fusion framework.

Existing evidence shows that weighted fusion (config_027) outperforms concat fusion, and scvi_n200 RNA encoder (config_027) is better than pca_n2000 (config_032). This experiment tests whether replacing resnet50 with imagenet_vit_l image encoder (while keeping scvi_n200 RNA, avgpool aggregation, and weighted fusion) improves performance, isolating the impact of image representation. It balances exploration of critical components (image encoder) with exploitation of proven effective settings (weighted fusion, scvi_n200).

Existing evidence shows that weighted fusion (config_027, 0.6776 accuracy) outperforms concat fusion, but aggregation method (avgpool vs transformer) remains untested. This experiment tests whether switching to transformer aggregation (a key design choice) with the same RNA/image encoders and weighted fusion (from config_027) could further improve performance. It isolates the effect of aggregation while building on the promising weighted fusion approach.

Existing evidence shows that config_049 (transformer aggregation + weighted fusion) achieves the highest accuracy so far. This experiment tests whether replacing the RNA encoder (scvi_n200 → pca_n2000) while keeping other components identical (resnet50 image encoder, transformer aggregation, weighted fusion) affects performance. This isolates the RNA encoder's impact on the top-performing configuration, addressing uncertainty about whether encoder choice is critical under these settings.

Existing evidence shows config_049 (transformer aggregation, weighted fusion) achieves the highest accuracy. This experiment tests whether the image encoder (imagenet_vit_l vs resnet50) impacts performance while keeping RNA encoder (scvi_n200), aggregation, and fusion consistent. It isolates the effect of the image encoder, a critical design choice, to determine if upgrading to a larger model improves performance.

Existing evidence shows that transformer aggregation and weighted fusion (config_044: 0.725 accuracy) outperform other methods. This experiment tests whether using pca_n2000 RNA encoder (vs scvi_n200 in config_044) with the same image encoder (imagenet_vit_l), aggregation, and fusion maintains high performance. It isolates the RNA encoder's impact while keeping other critical components fixed, addressing uncertainty about encoder choice.

The existing evidence shows that transformer aggregation and weighted fusion yield higher accuracy (e.g., config_044: 0.725). This experiment tests pca_n2000 RNA encoder with transformer aggregation and concat fusion, isolating the effect of RNA representation and aggregation method. It clarifies whether pca_n2000 RNA (vs scvi_n200) performs comparably with transformer aggregation, which is critical for balancing exploration and exploitation.

Existing evidence shows that transformer aggregation and weighted fusion (config_044) achieve the highest accuracy so far. This experiment tests whether switching to concat fusion (while keeping RNA encoder, image encoder, and aggregation method the same) affects performance, isolating the impact of fusion strategy. It balances exploitation of current high-performing components with exploration of critical design choices.
